source_of_truth: Read by hand. The 01-class defect (a module reaching into billing's private internal/calc) is written two ways: (A) fulfillment/useFulfillment.ts imports it with an `as` alias, and (B) fulfillment/index.ts re-exports it with `export { priceLines } from '~/features/billing/internal/calc'`. Both lines carry a specifier that points straight at billing's private file, so both are cross-module internal imports regardless of the surface syntax. The consumer page imports only through fulfillment/index.ts (the public entry), so the page is not at fault; the laundering is on the index line.

expected.rationale: Variant A: the `as calc` alias does not change the specifier; it resolves to billing/internal/calc.ts, a private file, not billing/index.ts.

Variant B: the re-export line is itself a cross-module edge whose specifier points at billing/internal/calc.ts; re-exporting another module's private symbol through your own index is still a boundary break, pinned on the index line that does it.

forbidden.why_not_a_defect: the page imports from ~/features/fulfillment, which resolves to fulfillment/index.ts (public entry); the page cannot be blamed for fulfillment laundering a private symbol, that fault is on fulfillment/index.ts
